content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Consider adding trusted domains to config/source_allowlist.txt

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know), 726 words, appropriate for the News category and word-count range (400-1200). Neutral, factual tone throughout — no editorializing, no sensationalism, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 6 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200) per manifest.json; sha256 of source-1 and source-0 spot-checked against manifest and matched. source-0 (changelog.complete.org, Goerzen's blog): the saved snapshot itself is NOT usable for review — it captured an Anubis anti-bot JavaScript challenge page ('Making sure you're not a bot!'), not the article, despite the 200 status code. Per protocol I used a live WebFetch on the same URL as the documented last-resort fallback (three separate targeted fetches, the last one requesting a verbatim quote) and cross-checked every fact attributed to this source against LWN's independently-verified snapshot text where overlap existed (the 'wasn't matching modern expectations' passage matched verbatim between the WebFetch result and the LWN snapshot, giving confidence the live fetch reflects the real page). Confirmed via WebFetch: 1981 Frank da Cruz/Bill Catchings design at Columbia; DEC-20/IBM mainframe, 8-bit-over-7-bit-links framing; 1982 port to MS-DOS/Unix; ISS and hurricane-sensor applications; Columbia's self-funded/commercial-licensing history keeping it out of Linux distros; 2011 cancellation and BSD open-sourcing; da Cruz's volunteer maintenance through his 2025 retirement; the exact Open Kermit creation quote ('to coordinate future development in the open and keep Kermit going') verified verbatim on a targeted re-fetch after an initial fetch failed to surface it; and 'nearly 2000 test cases in total.' source-1 (lwn.net, snapshot read directly): confirmed the verbatim quote 'the first release of this file-transfer utility in 15 years' and the full 'wasn't matching modern expectations' / character-set / line-ending-conversion passage the article says LWN quoted from Goerzen — matches character-for-character. source-2 (github.com/OpenKermit/ckermit release notes, snapshot read directly): confirmed verbatim 'Over 1700 test cases are being run', the IPv6/IPv4-fallback description, the CVE-2025-68920 description ('insecure defaults that previously would let a malicious remote kermit server perform actions on your local workstation'), the SET FILE COLLISION BACKUP-to-REJECT change and its '.bashrc' rationale verbatim, the transfer-mode automatic-to-manual change and its 'override the binary file type' rationale verbatim, 'last full release, 9.0.302 in 2011', gkermit/E-Kermit/9.0.302 compatibility-test claim, and both da Cruz dedication quotes ('directly involved with Kermit for 44 years... 1981... through 2025' and 'I know of no other Open Source project where the founder remains so personally involved for so long') verbatim. source-3 (nvd.nist.gov, snapshot read directly): confirmed CVSS 3.1 Base Score 8.9 HIGH (vector AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:L), CWE-862 Missing Authorization, and 'through 10.0 Beta.12' as the affected version range — all as the article states. source-4 (kermitproject.org/nasa.html, snapshot read directly): confirmed verbatim 'The MSG laptop has a copy of Kermit 95 installed via a CD-ROM which was launched with the CSLM-2 hardware in December, 2002' and that this laptop operated aboard the International Space Station. source-5 (openkermit.org, snapshot read directly): confirmed verbatim 'After the retirement of one of Kermit's founders after 44 years, Open Kermit is carrying it forward.'
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Central verification target #1 — the divergent test-count figures: confirmed each figure is attributed to the correct, separate source and NOT compound-cited. The article's sentence structure cites 'Over 1700 test cases are being run' to '[the GitHub release notes]' (a hyperlinked citation to source-2, verbatim match) and separately states Goerzen 'described the combined unit and end-to-end suites in his own post as running "nearly 2000 test cases in total"' (verified via WebFetch of source-0). No single footnote or sentence conflates the two figures under one citation; the bot correctly read this as two different counts from two different documents (GitHub CI test count vs. Goerzen's own total across unit+e2e suites) rather than a contradiction to average or pick one from. Central verification target #2 — CVE-2025-68920: every specific (CVSS 8.9 HIGH, CWE-862, 'through 10.0 Beta.12', the exact GitHub-release-notes description of the flaw, the SET FILE COLLISION and transfer-mode fixes) traces character-for-character to source-2 and source-3 as quoted above. Central verification target #3 — the 'first full release in 15 years' / 2011 comparison: verified character-for-character via source-1 (LWN's exact quoted sentence) and source-2 ('last full release, 9.0.302 in 2011'), both read directly from snapshot; August 2026 minus 2011 = 15 years, consistent with the LWN dateline (August 3, 2026). No fabricated or hallucinated specifics found anywhere in the body.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. The 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags open questions (distro packaging plans, migration timeline) rather than speculating.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ (all months) for any prior Kermit/C-Kermit coverage — none found (grep -rli "kermit" returned no results). Genuinely new topic, no overlap with recently published articles.
editor_notes.source_allowlist_resolution: The automated script's sole finding was that changelog.complete.org, openkermit.org, and kermitproject.org are not on config/source_allowlist.txt. I evaluated each and added all three: changelog.complete.org is John Goerzen's personal blog and the primary first-party announcement for his own release, directly analogous to the hacdias.com precedent (2026-08-02, Henrique Dias's blog as primary source for his own project's announcement). openkermit.org is the official site of the project itself, managed by Goerzen, analogous to already-listed maintainer/organization primary sources (temporal.io, aalto.fi). kermitproject.org is Columbia's original, long-standing Kermit Project archive (the NASA/ISS case study cited dates to 2003), a credible institutional primary-source archive. All three additions are documented with rationale comments in config/source_allowlist.txt under a 2026-08-04 batch heading. This resolved the only warning the automated script raised, so no corrections record is needed.
editor_notes.suspicious_patterns_check: manifest.json shows suspicious_patterns: null for all 6 sources. I independently re-scanned every decompressed snapshot for phrases like 'ignore previous instructions', 'AI agent', 'large language model', 'you are an AI', 'system prompt', 'do not tell the user' — no matches found in any of the 6 snapshots. No prompt-injection content present.
concerns: source-0's saved snapshot (sources/2026-08/c-kermit-11-ships-as-first-full-release-in-15-years-modernizing-the-45-year-old-file-transfer-protocol/source-0.html.gz) captured an Anubis anti-bot JavaScript challenge page rather than the real article content, despite a 200 status code and no error field in the manifest. This means the committed provenance snapshot for that one source is not independently re-checkable content — I verified the underlying facts via live WebFetch instead (three targeted fetches, documented above) and cross-referenced overlapping claims against the LWN snapshot, but a future auditor reading only the committed source-0 snapshot will see a bot-challenge page, not the cited article. Recommend the snapshot fetcher special-case Anubis/similar JS-challenge responses as a soft failure (comparable to a 403) rather than treating a 200 status as sufficient to mark the snapshot good.
recommendations: Consider having the snapshot fetcher detect known anti-bot challenge pages (e.g. Anubis's 'Making sure you're not a bot!' interstitial) by content signature, not just HTTP status, and either retry via the Archive.org fallback path or flag the source as unverifiable so reviewers don't have to discover it manually.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, thoroughly sourced submission. Both divergent test-count figures are correctly and separately attributed rather than conflated. CVE-2025-68920 details and the 15-years/2011 release-gap comparison verify character-for-character against the cited sources. The only defect found (source-0's snapshot capturing a bot-challenge page instead of real content) was worked around via a documented live-fetch fallback and does not implicate the article's accuracy. The allowlist warning was resolved by adding three legitimate primary sources following established precedent. Approve without corrections.
